extractedItems.ruleName: Ball lost in abnormal course conditions
extractedItems.group: Ball lost in abnormal course conditions
extractedItems.title: Free relief for lost ball in abnormal course conditions
extractedItems.question: If you lose your ball in an area you’re sure is abnormal course conditions, what are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Play a new ball from the tee with a penalty
Take free relief from where your ball last crossed the edge of the abnormal area
Drop another ball anywhere you like, no penalty
You have to search for your ball for 10 minutes

extractedItems.explanation: You take free relief from the spot where your ball last crossed the edge of the abnormal course conditions.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer standing next to a marked area of abnormal course condition, about to drop a ball where she believes her ball last entered the area, with no penalty.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Junior girl golfer about to drop a ball at the edge of an abnormal course condition area.

extractedItems.title: Ball lands on the wrong green
extractedItems.question: Your ball lands on a practice green or another putting green for a different hole. What must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies to save time
Pick up the ball and throw it off the green
Take free relief by dropping the ball off the green, no closer to the hole
Ask for a penalty and replay the shot

extractedItems.explanation: You must take free relief and drop the ball off the wrong green, no closer to the hole.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy standing beside a wrong green, preparing to drop his ball off the edge of the green, holding a wedge.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Junior boy golfer about to drop a ball near the edge of a different putting green.

extractedItems.ruleName: Divots, tractor ruts, bald patches, etc.
extractedItems.group: Divots, tractor ruts, bald patches, etc.
extractedItems.title: Playing from a divot, rut or bald patch
extractedItems.question: If your ball lands in a deep divot or a tractor rut, what are your options?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable (with a penalty)
Always get free relief
Move the ball to the nearest perfect grass
Ask for a re-do with no penalty

extractedItems.explanation: You must play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable and take a penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer looking down at his golf ball resting in a deep divot on the fairway, preparing to play the difficult shot.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Junior golfer faced with a golf ball lying in a divot on the fairway.

reviewedItems.ruleName: Ball lost in abnormal course conditions
reviewedItems.group: Ball lost in abnormal course conditions
reviewedItems.title: Free relief for lost ball in abnormal course conditions
reviewedItems.question: You are certain your ball is lost in an area marked as abnormal course conditions (like ground under repair), but you can’t find it. What are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Play a new ball from the tee with a penalty
Take free relief by dropping a ball at the spot where your original ball last crossed the edge of the abnormal course condition
Drop another ball anywhere on the course without penalty
Search for your ball for 10 minutes

reviewedItems.explanation: If you are certain your ball is lost in abnormal course conditions, you may take free relief by dropping a ball at the point where the ball last crossed the edge of that area, with no penalty.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy in the rough next to a clearly marked ground under repair area, preparing to drop a golf ball just outside the painted line, with his iron club ready.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy golfer about to drop a ball next to a ground under repair area in the rough.

reviewedItems.title: Ball lands on the wrong green
reviewedItems.question: If your ball comes to rest on a putting green that’s not the one for the hole you’re playing, what should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies to save time
Pick up the ball and throw it off the green
Take free relief by dropping the ball off the green, no closer to the hole
Ask for a penalty and replay the shot

reviewedItems.explanation: You must take free relief by dropping your ball off the wrong green, no closer to the hole, and may not play from another putting green.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl on a putting green that is not the correct green for her hole, preparing to drop a golf ball just off the green with a wedge.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl golfer about to drop a ball from the edge of a putting green, preparing for free relief.

reviewedItems.ruleName: Divots, tractor ruts, bald patches, etc.
reviewedItems.group: Divots, tractor ruts, bald patches, etc.
reviewedItems.title: Playing from a divot, rut or bald patch
reviewedItems.question: Your ball lands in a deep divot or a tractor rut on the fairway. Which of these is correct?

choices.text: You must play the ball as it lies or take an unplayable lie and add a penalty
You always get free relief
You can move the ball to some good grass without penalty
You are allowed to rehit your shot with no penalty

reviewedItems.explanation: You have to play the ball as it lies, or declare it unplayable and take a penalty stroke—there is no free relief just for a divot or rut.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl in a navy top and red bottoms, addressing a golf ball lying in a deep divot on a fairway under an overcast sky, holding an iron club and ready to play.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl golfer in navy and red about to play a ball from a fairway divot.
